goal: On Claude Code, a literal-user imm-run entry mints a session- and workspace-bound entry token. Enrollment and unattended batch start keep one native gate per entry, because a same-uid model write can forge the token; under a live token stale batch retirement and same-Host recovery open no gate. A confirmed batch start prints a non-blocking execution manifest, and the token is invalidated by session exit, workspace change or a Stop-boundary pause (Spec D1-D4, D6, D11; ADR 0025).

acceptance.assertion: After a UserPromptSubmit carrying a literal imm-run entry, enroll and start_unattended_batch each open exactly one native gate, and a declined gate claims nothing even with a live token; a later retire_stale_batch under that token completes with no elicitation/create request and records a confirmation_ref of kind entry_token still bound to the plan digest; a rework-exit confirmation still opens elicitation with its exits.

Each of these is refused with no Kernel mutation: an authority tool call with no prior literal entry; a call whose session id differs from the minting session; a call after SessionEnd; a call from a different workspace realpath; a call after the run paused at the Stop boundary; a tool argument that supplies a token or native_decision field.

A confirmed start_unattended_batch result carries a manifest listing every child's task id, risk, scope summary and verification commands; a lane-mode batch dialog under a live token still offers the Lane revision delegation choice; and the token stays live across a same-session continuation until the bound run is terminal.
